purpose: Pirfenidone is used to treat a serious lung condition called idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, or IPF. This condition causes scar tissue to build up in the lungs over time, making it harder to breathe. This medication helps slow down that scarring process so your lungs can keep working as well as possible for longer.
how_it_works: Your lungs can sometimes produce too much scar tissue, which stiffens them and makes breathing difficult. Pirfenidone works by blocking certain signals in your body that tell cells to create that scar tissue. Think of it like a brake pedal that slows down the scarring process, helping to preserve your lung function over time.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, upset stomach, loss of appetite, tiredness, and skin reactions to sunlight such as redness or a rash. Some people also experience dizziness, headache, or diarrhea. Taking the medication with food and using sunscreen daily can help reduce many of these effects.
warnings: This medication can make your skin very sensitive to sunlight, so it is very important to wear sunscreen and protective clothing every day when going outdoors. Avoid tanning beds completely. Pirfenidone can also affect your liver, so your doctor will do regular blood tests to check your liver. Tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, or dark urine. Avoid smoking, as it can reduce how well the medication works.
typical_dosing: You usually start at a lower dose and slowly increase it over a few weeks to help your body adjust. The typical full dose is 3 capsules taken 3 times a day with food, adding up to 9 capsules per day. Your doctor will guide you through the dose increase schedule to help minimize side effects.
